title: Pride the Destroyer, Christ the Redeemer
summary: Pride is the deadliest sin and leads to all the others. Speak up, and above all love people boldly with the gospel, which is the power of God.
exhortation: 1 John 2:16 says, "For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world."

We find ourselves in what some call Pride Month, when the world celebrates sinful actions that God calls destructive. And it's striking how they hit the nail on the head in calling it pride. Pride really is the deadliest of all sins, and it leads to all the others. As Romans says, people not only do these things but give approval to those who practice them.

It starts by refusing God: "There is no God." Then we believe a lie. And since our hearts must worship something, we turn a lifestyle or whatever it is into an idol. Most frightening of all, God gives us what we want. Romans 1:24-25 says, "God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity... because they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever! Amen."

So how do we respond as Christians? We should speak up, not just to protect ourselves, but to protect those caught up in it and those affected by it, because it is destructive for everyone, especially those who have been deceived. As citizens we should seek the good of those around us whenever we have the opportunity to vote. And last and most important, we should love these people by being bold with the gospel, trusting that God is working despite how dark things look or how hostile people may be toward Christianity, and believing that the gospel is the power of God.

Let me end with an encouraging story from our church in Pasadena several years ago. A woman was out watering her front lawn when her neighbor walked up and said, "Hi, I'm transgender." She answered, "Hi, I'm a Christian." I love that. She didn't recoil, and she didn't unload all her opinions. She invited him into her home. They walked and talked together, and he spent Christmas and Thanksgiving with her family. She told me she never hid what she believed, and there were times he got frustrated and they disagreed, but she had built a bridge because she cared about him. This is God's grace at work. We should be sober-minded, and we don't have to engage someone who is hateful or violent. But when you see an opportunity like this, pray that God opens your eyes.
prayer: Lord, we were all dead in our trespasses and sins, with no hope except that you breathe life into dead bones. Thank you, Jesus, for breathing life into us. Destroy whatever small view of you has put limits on your salvation, limits we might never say out loud but still think and feel. There is no situation your grace cannot completely transform and no sin your mercy cannot cover.

Give us a mighty faith in the great salvation you have brought about. May we see it everywhere we go, in every interaction and with every person we meet. Help us listen for your Spirit's prompting so that we speak and enter in, so that your grace may cover the earth. What a privilege that we get to be part of it. Thank you, Lord. Amen.
